exact_identity.premise: C_plus = (x OR A), C_minus = (NOT x OR B), with literal-set(A) subseteq literal-set(B)
exact_identity.rewrite: C_plus AND C_minus == C_plus AND B
exact_identity.symmetric_case: If literal-set(B) subseteq literal-set(A), rewrite C_plus AND C_minus == A AND C_minus
exact_identity.reason: If B were false then A is false; the two parent clauses would force x and NOT x simultaneously. Thus the parents imply B. Conversely B implies (NOT x OR B), so replacing the larger parent by its resolvent body preserves equivalence.

important_boundary: This is a local exact CNF equivalence contraction, not a universal polynomial closure theorem and not evidence that P=NP.
